title: Bacterial spot of tomato and pepper on hot pepper

Header: Bacterial spot of tomato and pepper on hot pepper
Xanthomonas vesicatoria ( syn. Xanthomonas campestris pv. Vesicatoria bacterial leaf blight of tomato and pepper; bacterial spot of tomato

Prevention: Prevention
This disease is spread by infected- crop residues, seeds, plants, soil, through water/ rain splash, also by people touching sick plants.
Once the disease enters the field it is hard to control.
Use seeds treated with hot water or bleach, or clean seedlings
Rotate crops with non-host plants like cucurbits ( e.g. pumpkin, squash ) for about 2 years.
NOT with
Solanaceae crops ( e.g.
Tomato or
Eggplant/Melongene
Use cambered beds (Heavy clay soils) or ridges (Loamy/Sandy
Soils).
Place furrows in and around fields to improve soil drainage as the disease spreads in wet conditions
Use organic mulch to help prevent spread of the disease as it reduces water / soil splash
Use drip irrigation and avoid overhead sprinklers to prevent bacteria spread by water/soil splashes
Maintain good
N & K nutrition to help plants resist infection.
Do not use dolomitic limestone, as high
Mg predisposes plants to the disease.
Use calcium limestone
Remove older leaves, closest to the soil to reduce contact to soil
Monitoring: Monitor weekly from seedbed stage; extra care during wet conditions.
Examine leaves and fruit, start with leaves near the ground.
V-shaped areas along leaf margin, which turn brown and dry.b.
Brown, circular spots with yellow halos, between the veins.
They can join and dry out, to give a tattered leaf scorch appearance. c.
Vein blackening may extend down the leaves into stem. d.Fruit spots on the stem-end of fruit
Use a direct control measure upon early symptoms a & b listed above.
Consider when symptoms c & d are detected, direct control may be too late
Direct Control: Remove and bury/burn infected plants and weeds from in and around fields, up to flowering stage of crop.
Avoid infected material from contacting the rest of the crop during this activity.
Disinfect pruners and other tools by dipping in a commercial sanitizer, or a 1% bleach.
Avoid walking through wet field to not spread the disease

Direct
Control
Restrictions
Diseased plants cannot be cured.
Spraying will only help to prevent new infections of healthy plants.
Foliar spray every 7-14 days until crop flowering
When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
such as dosage, timing of application, pre
harvest interval, max number of sprays, restricted re
entry interval.
Always consult recent list of registered pesticide.
WHO toxicity class
II (Moderately acute hazardous to humans).

Toxic to aquatic organisms.
